idiom_name: std::function chain: filters as callables taking the next handler
implementation_notes: There is no framework-neutral filter mechanism in the standard library, so the structure is hand-written: a filter is any callable with the shape Response(Request&, const Next&), and the manager folds a vector of filters around the target in configuration order, each layer capturing the next one by value. std::function type-erases heterogeneous filters and costs one indirect call per layer; when the filter set is fixed at compile time, templates or tuples compose them with no indirection at all. Use this form when the target and the pipeline are yours.
pitfalls: A filter that captures the chain by reference dangles once the builder returns; capture the next handler by value, as above.
std::function allocates for captures above its small-buffer limit and every layer adds an indirect call; a long chain in a hot path is measurable.
Capturing per-request data in the composed chain is a data race in a multithreaded server - keep the chain immutable and shared, the request state separate.

variants.name: gRPC C++ server interceptors
variants.implementation_notes: For a gRPC server the framework owns the chain: derive from grpc::experimental::Interceptor, inspect the batch with QueryInterceptionHookPoint(...) for pre- and post-points (for example POST_RECV_INITIAL_METADATA before the handler, PRE_SEND_STATUS after it), and call methods->Proceed() to continue - not calling it short-circuits the RPC. Factories deriving from ServerInterceptorFactoryInterface are handed to the builder through builder.experimental().SetInterceptorCreators(...), and one interceptor instance is created per RPC. The API is still marked experimental, so pin the gRPC version you build against.
pitfalls: Forgetting methods->Proceed() hangs the RPC: interceptors are the chain, not the target.
One interceptor instance per RPC means the interceptor must keep per-call state in its own object, not in the factory.
The API is experimental: header paths and hook-point names change between gRPC releases, so isolate the interceptor in one translation unit.
